speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) what is the status of the Postal Quality of Service framework review; (b) how many complaints has SingPost received about missing mails in the past year; and (c) how many of these missing mail cases have been resolved.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) in the past 36 months, how many complaints have been received on misuse of failed postal delivery notices when recipients are home; and (b) whether IMDA investigates these complaints to ensure compliance of the Postal Quality of Service framework.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: SingPost has to meet the Postal Quality of Service (QoS) standards set by the Info-communications Media Development Authority (IMDA) for letter delivery.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: SingPost also provides other services, such as advertisement mail and parcel delivery, that are not subject to IMDA's Postal QoS standards.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The recent lapses by SingPost involve services covered by the Postal QoS standards, and those that are not.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: For letter delivery, the QoS standards are: to deliver 99% of local basic letters destined for the Central Business District (CBD), and 98% for those destined for non-CBD areas, by the next working day; and 100% for all letters by the second working day.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: SingPost has accepted IMDA's decision and committed to improve its service delivery standards, including its QoS performance.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: IMDA is reviewing SingPost's performance for letter delivery in 2018.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: SingPost has investigated each complaint and has apologised to the complainant whenever there was a confirmed service lapse, and redelivered mail that was found.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: IMDA has also reviewed its QoS standards for letter delivery and has decided to maintain them.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah also asked about complaints relating to consumers receiving failed delivery notices even when there was someone at home.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: These pertain to the delivery of parcels and registered articles.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: SingPost is unable to provide the specific number of complaints it receives on failed delivery notices.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Nonetheless, we believe that there are likely to be more incidents which were not formally reported.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: SingPost's Board and management agree with my Ministry and IMDA that a thorough review of its operations and manpower has to be made even as it takes immediate steps to remedy the service lapses.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: They have reaffirmed SingPost’s commitment to prioritise improvements to service delivery standards and the welfare of its workforce.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: SingPost has already made a start by announcing measures, such as extending parcel delivery to Saturdays, cutting back on advertisement mail delivery and improving staff remuneration.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: SingPost has pointed out that the popularity of e-commerce has significantly increased the volume of parcels.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As a result, it has to deliver 38,000 items daily which cannot fit into letter boxes and its postmen have to now conduct more deliveries for parcels.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This works out to an average of 35 to 45 doorstep deliveries per postman per day in Singapore's urban landscape with many high-rise Housing and Development Board (HDB) blocks and condominiums, in addition to delivering letters to letter boxes.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: My Ministry and IMDA are of the view that SingPost must make itself ready for this new operating environment.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The work of the postman is labour-intensive and has become more so over the years.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: My Ministry and IMDA are of the view that, even as SingPost remedies its service lapses, its postal workforce should be treated fairly and be well-equipped to perform their job.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Where necessary, IMDA will provide support to SingPost in the training of postmen, delivery process re-engineering, deployment of technological solutions and infrastructure upgrades to optimise its delivery process.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It may take time before the gaps in SingPost's service delivery are fully addressed.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The SingPost Board and management know there is hard work ahead and have told us that they are committed to work together with my Ministry and IMDA.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Further regulatory action from IMDA can be expected, as it reviews SingPost’s letter delivery performance for 2018 and beyond, investigates infringements under the Postal Services Act and considers additional regulatory standards.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I filed a Parliamentary Question (PQ) in February 2017 here, on letters frequently delivered to the wrong addresses.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Since then, the situation has gone from bad to worse.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Residents are now not just complaining that letters are delivered to the wrong addresses, there are also many complaints that the letters they are expecting do not arrive, and the worst was towards end of last year.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: That is why I filed a question again.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: My first question is: did SingPost foresee the seasonal peak and the surge of e-commerce and planned for them?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Why has it become much worse at the end of last year?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Are there shortages in manpower and, if there are, is there any study into the remuneration package and welfare for postmen and other ground service staff?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, did they do a remuneration package study?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: My second question is: there is only one postal service company in Singapore and it is doing essential service.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: How do we ensure that they are not complacent?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Because this issue has been brought up in Parliament before.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It is not getting better but getting worse.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, it shows that maybe they are complacent.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Earlier, the Senior Minister of State mentioned about regulatory requirement and I have also read on several occasions that the Ministry had implied or mentioned the revoking of licence.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Are there any plans to issue more than one licence so that there is competition?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, we may want to look into having more than one postal services provider in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah mentioned six supplementary questions; I counted five.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But if I leave out any, she is welcomed to ask again.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I will take her last question first, which is, what actions for the residents of Yishun.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We hope that this would address at least some of the concerns, but IMDA will be monitoring this very closely.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah has also asked about the situation in Yishun as of the end of last year as her first question.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: She has also asked whether SingPost had planned for the seasonal peaks and what has it been doing to cope with the operating environment.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: SingPost has talked about seasonal peaks and about the changing proportion of parcels to letters.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We are of the view that this is something which it, as the service provider and the operator, should plan for and ensure that its workforce is properly remunerated, properly trained and equipped to do this job.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As for the status of SingPost as the postal service provider, I believe the next two questions that Er Dr Lee had mentioned pertain to this.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Under our current framework, we have one public postal licensee, that is, SingPost.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But it is not the only ones who are licensed to deliver basic letters.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As the public postal licensee, what they need to do is, in addition to delivering letters, they have to maintain a set of universal service obligations (USOs).

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: These include, for instance, the maintenance of posting boxes, the issuance of stamps and there is an obligation to deliver basic letters from and to anyone within Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Those are the obligations tied to being the public postal licensee.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This does not mean they have a monopoly on the delivery of basic letter services.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This segment of the market has also been opened up.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As explained, there are now four in total.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As for parcel delivery, this is also a very open and competitive segment.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We have many companies that are doing parcel and door-to-door delivery.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Er Dr Lee has asked about the quantum of the fine and whether that is considered sufficient.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I have described earlier in the main reply there are several types of QoS that the public postal licensee has to abide by.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In terms of determining the actual quantum per count, IMDA would take into account factors, such as whether there are aggravating factors, for instance, has there been repeated failures, and also, mitigating factors, for instance, whether or not the delay time is longer or shorter.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We completely agree with Er Dr Lee that relying on fines is not sufficient.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As I have mentioned, regulatory action is ongoing.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But very importantly, other measures also need to be taken.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We are glad to see that SingPost has owned the issue and has announced steps in the right direction, for instance, by extending delivery hours, by relooking at remuneration for its workforce and so forth.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: At the same time, the use of technology must continue.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is something that IMDA has been in constant discussion with SingPost on, and, in fact, in previous years, have also required SingPost to take on technological upgrade so that its postal workforce can do its job better.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The next question that Er Dr Lee has asked touches on who gets to deliver basic letters.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, I have covered that when I explained the overall framework.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: My residents have also told me that they often do not receive letters even from my constituency office.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: In other words, postal service is the cash cow for SingPost.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: So, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State, is it the case where SingPost is under-investing in postal services while they try to take some money to diversify their business?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I believe that Mr Ang Wei Neng's question is also something that should be asked of SingPost by its shareholders.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I understand that these are also the issues that the shareholders should hold SingPost to account for.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In terms of under-investing, I shall not comment on this specific issue.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: However, we can also take cognisance of the steps that SingPost has talked about, in terms of paying more attention to the postal workforce, in ensuring that the operations are right, in extending the delivery hours.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, those steps that they have mentioned are indicative of what SingPost's own diagnosis of the problem is.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We will continue to work very closely with SingPost.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We will also continue to monitor and regulate.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: While we are still waiting for technological solutions, such as the use of drones to deliver mail, I wonder if the Ministry could consider or help to facilitate alternate delivery agents and systems for now.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In the Central Community Development Council (CDC), we tried a drop-mail system where we employed senior citizens who are still healthy to drop mail in their localities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We found the outcomes to be quite good in accuracy and the speed was very fast, maybe better than SingPost.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The CDC does not have the ability to scale it, but I believe there is a good potential there to create reliable delivery systems, employing seniors and also graduands of Special Education schools and others who may not be able to have other forms of jobs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I wonder if the Ministry and other related agencies would be interested in helping us organise this so that we can scale this kind of system and create interim jobs that might be meaningful, and also provide opportunities for seniors and others to build better health and earn some pocket money.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I shall ask IMDA to work closely with her CDC to understand this pilot scheme that she has started and to see how this can improve postal services.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is a trial that SingPost is also a part of, to see whether there can be better solutions for the last-mile delivery of parcels which may be too large to fit into letter boxes.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I just have a question, and this pertains to the timeline.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I understand that some time may be needed for SingPost to address the gaps and as the Ministry of Communications and Information considers additional regulation, may I know if there is a timeline for both these aspects?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In the meantime, what else might we be able to expect to ensure that the letter delivery performance will still be upheld?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Otherwise, they are overstressing the current working postmen.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: That is why, sometimes, you will find that there are other consequences.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: For the second question, just now, the Senior Minister of State mentioned about thorough review with SingPost.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I think they are overstressed; they work very hard.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I think the Senior Minister of State did not answer one of my questions.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I asked under what circumstances would the licence be revoked.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: First, Er Dr Lee has asked about staffing issues.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I think that by announcing its plans to hire more postmen, SingPost is acknowledging that there are vacancies and I believe it is not only restricted to the Woodlands distribution centre.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We believe that with SingPost's intention to also review remuneration for the staff, we hope that these vacancies will be easier to fill than they currently are now.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In terms of the concern on manpower, indeed, we share Er Dr Lee's concerns about the importance of maintaining the well-being of the postal workforce.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is the reason why it is not just about tightening requirements and levying the penalties, but also monitoring very closely to ensure that, first of all, the workforce is adequately trained and prepared for the job that they have to do.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is certainly a priority for my Ministry and also for IMDA.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In terms of the circumstances under which the licence for being the public postal licensee will be revoked, first of all, I want to state that we do need an operator to maintain the universal service obligations.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As I have mentioned, it is not just about delivery of the letters.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It is about maintaining the posting boxes, it is about issuance of stamps, it is also about having somebody who undertakes to deliver and collect letters from anywhere in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: What we currently have is a set of QoS standards to monitor the delivery of letters.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: However, we are very conscious of the pain points that consumers have reported, including pain points concerning services that are not covered by the QoS, and this is the reason why IMDA is now also considering additional regulatory standards.
